faq.q: What is included in the Marbella bottom fishing half-day charter?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Fishing rods, bait, and tackle are provided. The catch and cook option adds a chef to prepare your fish on board or at a nearby restaurant.

faq.q: Which boats are available for bottom fishing charters?
faq.a: Our bottom fishing charters typically use the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax). Both depart from Puerto Banús and are well-equipped for fishing. For larger groups, inquire about other boats via WhatsApp.

faq.q: What fish can we catch on a bottom fishing trip in Marbella?
faq.a: Common catches include sea bream, grouper, snapper, red mullet, and horse mackerel. The waters off Marbella are rich with rocky reefs and sandy bottoms, providing excellent bottom fishing from spring through autumn.

faq.q: How does the catch and cook option work?
faq.a: After your half-day trip, your catch is cleaned and prepared by a chef. You can enjoy it grilled or fried on board, or at a local restaurant near Puerto Banús. The option adds a delicious end to your fishing adventure.

faq.q: Is the catch and cook option available for all boat sizes?
faq.a: Yes, it works with any boat in our fleet, but is most popular on the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 for half-day trips. For larger groups, the Mangusta 80 (12 pax) or Azimut 58 Flybridge can be arranged with a chef.

faq.q: Do I need a fishing license for a bottom fishing charter in Marbella?
faq.a: No, your license is covered by the charter. The skipper holds all necessary permits. Just bring your enthusiasm and sunscreen.

faq.q: What is the best time of year for bottom fishing in Marbella?
faq.a: Bottom fishing is productive year-round, but the best catches occur from April to October when water temperatures are warmer. Summer months offer calm seas and longer daylight hours.

faq.q: Can we keep the fish we catch?
faq.a: Yes, you can keep your catch. The catch and cook option lets you eat it fresh, or you can take it home. The skipper will advise on size limits and sustainable practices.

data.body_html:
Book a Marbella bottom fishing half-day charter with a catch and cook option for an unforgettable day on the Mediterranean. Depart from Puerto Banús, target local species like sea bream and grouper, and enjoy your fresh catch prepared by a chef. Prices start at €749 for 9 guests on the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39, including skipper, gear, and drinks. Whether you're a seasoned angler or a beginner, this experience offers authentic fishing in the golden waters off Marbella.

Why Choose a Marbella Bottom Fishing Half-Day Charter?

A half-day bottom fishing charter is perfect for those who want a focused fishing experience without committing to a full day. You'll explore rocky reefs and sandy bottoms near Marbella, where fish like snapper and red mullet thrive. The catch and cook option adds a unique twist: your catch is prepared on board or at a local restaurant, turning your fishing trip into a culinary treat. With boats departing from Puerto Banús, you're minutes from prime fishing grounds.

Our Boats for Bottom Fishing Charters

We offer two excellent boats for half-day bottom fishing trips, both departing from Puerto Banús:

Both include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and all fishing gear. For larger groups, inquire about the Mangusta 80 (12 pax) or Azimut 58 Flybridge via WhatsApp.

What to Expect on Your Bottom Fishing Trip

Your half-day charter begins at Puerto Banús. The skipper navigates to proven fishing spots near the coast, such as the reefs off Cabopino or the deeper waters near Estepona. You'll use bottom fishing techniques with bait and tackle provided. Expect to catch sea bream, grouper, snapper, and horse mackerel. The trip includes soft drinks, beer, and light snacks. After fishing, the catch and cook option lets you enjoy your fish grilled or fried, often at a beachside restaurant near the Golden Mile.

Catch and Cook: A Unique Dining Experience

The catch and cook option elevates your charter. After the fishing, a chef cleans and prepares your catch. You can dine on board or at a local restaurant in Puerto Banús. The chef uses simple Mediterranean flavours—olive oil, lemon, garlic—to highlight the freshness. This option is available for all boats and is especially popular on the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39. It's a memorable way to end your day on the water.

Best Fishing Spots Near Marbella

Marbella's coastline offers excellent bottom fishing. Key spots include the rocky bottoms near Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, the sandy grounds off Río Verde, and the deeper reefs between Marbella Marina and Sotogrande. The skipper knows these areas intimately and adjusts based on weather and fish activity. Summer months (May to September) provide the best conditions, with calm seas and active fish.

What's Included and What to Bring

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Fishing rods, bait, and tackle are provided. Bring sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, and a light jacket. For the catch and cook option, no extra gear is needed—just your appetite.

Booking and Pricing

Prices start at €749 for a 2-hour trip on the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39, with longer half-day options available. The catch and cook option is priced on request. For larger groups, the Mangusta 80 (€4,719 minimum 4h, includes a free jet ski) or other boats are available. Contact us via WhatsApp for custom quotes.
